# dsh-mindmap
English | 简体中文
Open, edit and export mind maps in the DeepSeek Harness right sidebar.
## Formats
| Format | Open | Edit & save | Export `.mm` |

| `.xmind` (XMind 8 / Zen) | ✅ | read-only | ✅ |
| `.mm` (FreeMind) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `.opml` | ✅ | ✅
For `.xmind`, the viewer reads either `content.json` (XMind Zen / XMind 8) or `content.xml` and keep
s the topic hierarchy, notes and collapse state. XMind themes, relationship lines, attachments and o
ther advanced content are not rendered, and exporting to `.mm` keeps only the structure.
Because `.xmind` is read-only, the viewer offers **Convert to editable .mm**: it writes a sibling `.
mm` file (asking before overwriting) and opens it for editing.
## Install
### From npm (recommended)
Open **Plugins** in DSH, choose **Add plugin** (some builds label it **Install bundle**), and enter:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
> The npm package is `@jeffreylong/dsh-mindmap`. Do **not** install the bare name `dsh-mindmap` — th
at is a different, unrelated package. After installation the plugin row is labelled `dsh-mindmap`, a
nd its internal row id is `jeffreylong-dsh-mindmap`, so both can coexist.
Choose **Enable now**, then reload the Harness window.
If your npm registry is a private mirror that does not proxy npmjs.org, point this scope at the publ
registry is a private mirror that does not proxy npmjs.org, point this scope at the public registry:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
From a terminal you can install the package into a profile with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
and enable `dsh-mindmap` on the Plugins page.
### From source
1. Clone this repository:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
2. In DSH, open **Plugins** → **Install bundle** and point it at the cloned directory. You can also

ask an agent to call `plugin_manager install_bundle` with that path.
3. Reload the Harness window. I
f clicking a `.mm` file still opens the editor instead of this viewer, restart DSH once - the client
injection list is read at startup. The save route and both agent tools live in the Host process, so
restart DSH after installing or updating the bundle.
There is no build step: DSH loads `client.js` directly as a browser module.
## Usage
- Click a `.mm`, `.opml`, `.km`, `.vym` or `.xmind` file in the workspace file tree to open it in th

e right sidebar.
- Double-click a topic to rename it. `Tab` adds a child, `Enter` adds a sibling, `F

2` renames, `Delete` deletes.
- Right-click a topic for a context menu: new child, new sibling, rena

me, collapse and delete.
- One floating bar at the bottom holds the controls: undo/redo, collapse-al

l, zoom out / percentage / zoom in, fit, format, save, convert and export.
- The format panel offers
four structures (right, balanced, down, left) and three branch-line styles (curved, straight, elbow

). These are view preferences, not written into the file.
- The lower-left corner starts with the sm
all `EN` / `中` toggle, followed by the topic count, read-only note and unsaved state. The bar itself

only holds the action buttons; hover an icon to see its tooltip. It defaults to Chinese.
- `⌘Z` / `
⇧⌘Z` undo and redo, `Space` collapses or expands, `Ctrl`/`⌘` + wheel zooms at the cursor, the wheel

pans, drag to pan.
- `⌘S` or the save button in the bottom bar saves. `.xmind` has no save button; u
se **Convert to editable .mm** (writes a sibling file) or **Export to .mm** (download).
Saving overwrites editable files that already exist. The `.xmind` conversion is the one path that cr
eates a new file, and only next to the original `.xmind`; it never overwrites without confirmation.
## Agent tools
The bundle also registers two host tools, so an agent can read and edit a map without moving raw XML
through the conversation:
- `mindmap_outline({ path, includeNotes?, maxDepth? })` returns an indented outline with stable ids
and the file version:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- `mindmap_apply({ path, baseVersion, ops })` applies node-level changes atomically. Pass the versio
n from `mindmap_outline`; if the file changed, nothing is written and the tool asks for a re-read.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Both tools accept workspace-relative or absolute paths. Writes are fenced by the session's sandbox p
olicy: `workspace-write` confines them to the session workspace, full access does not. `.xmind` is r
eadable but not writable; convert it to `.mm` first. The viewer does not watch the file, so close an
d reopen the tab to see an agent's edit.
## How it works
- The client half registers a native `sidebar.right.pane.tab` type with an extension-priority addres
s glob that is longer than `dsh-resource://file/**`, so it outranks `dsh-better-sidebar`'s editor fo

r these extensions while still coexisting with it.
- Files are read with `ctx.remote.workspaceFiles.

readBytes`.
- Rendering is hand-written SVG: no third-party renderer and no bundling step.
- Saving
goes through the host route `POST /dsh-mindmap/save`: connection fence, extension allow-list, 8 MiB
body limit and an optimistic version check (`409` on conflict). The session's sandbox policy decides
whether the target path is writable. When the route is unreachable, the viewer falls back to downlo

ading the file.
- Performance guards: XMind archives only inflate `content.json` / `content.xml` (24
MiB per entry, 32 MiB total); text files over 8 MiB and maps over 20,000 topics are rejected. Panni
ng moves the SVG transform without re-rendering, wheel zoom is frame-throttled, nodes are memoized,
label measurements are cached, and undo history shrinks on large maps.
## Limitations

- `.mmap`, `.mindnode` and `.emmx` are not supported.
- Hard limits: 8 MiB for text formats, 20,000

topics, 24 MiB per XMind content entry. Larger files are refused rather than frozen.
- Maps above 4,
000 topics still render as one SVG; very large maps may feel slow even with the interaction optimiza

tions.
- XMind is read-only; exporting to `.mm` drops XMind styling and rich content.
- In a very na
rrow sidebar, **Fit** shrinks the whole map considerably. Zoom in and pan for detail.
